clue.text: Satanists' leader breaks mirror in church recess

indicators.note: one piece breaks into another, splitting it open to sit inside it

parts.note: to ape is to mirror or mimic someone

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Devil-worshippers' chief smashes a looking glass in a quiet corner of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mirror' looks like a noun but is the verb APE; the S from 'Satanists' leader' breaks into it.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the vaulted semicircular recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: One to depart this world like man strapped in tight?

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: the man is held within the word for tight, as if buckled in

parts.note: taut means tight
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man strapped tightly into his seat is about to leave Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depart this world' sounds like dying, but means leaving the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut travels into space, literally leaving the Earth behind.

clue.text: Country squire's first visionary sent heavenward

indicators.note: a word's first is its opening letter
in a down clue, sent upwards means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: airy means fanciful or visionary, as in airy-fairy schemes

explanation.surface: A rural squire is the first dreamer to be launched skyward.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East.

clue.text: Challenging type seen in different locations around clubs

indicators.note: the reshuffled letters sit around the clubs letter, enclosing it
the letters of the word are made different, put into a new order

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A provocative person turns up in various places with a set of golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges LOCATIONS into ICONOLAST, which goes 'around' C to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An iconoclast attacks cherished beliefs and institutions, so is a person who challenges convention.

clue.text: Mob down by 500 attending pub one used to open

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so the pub comes alongside
down by means reduced by, so the Roman numeral is taken away

parts.note: a crowd is a mob
D is 500 in Roman numerals
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A rabble, short of a few hundred, goes to the pub when it opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar is an iron lever used to prise things open, such as crates or doors.

clue.text: Invaders succeeded with right to enter Donne's island?

indicators.note: the right letter enters the phrase, going inside it

parts.note: John Donne wrote 'No man is an island', so in his phrase no man is an island
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A conquering force takes a poet's island, entitled to go ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: Donne's line 'No man is an island' lets 'Donne's island' stand for NO MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans invaded and conquered England in 1066.

clue.text: Involving a mystery whose point is concealed?

definitions.text: Involving a mystery whose point is concealed?

parts.words: Involving a mystery whose point is concealed?
parts.note: describes spy fiction, and literally a blade whose point is hidden under a garment

explanation.walkthrough: The 'point' is both the purpose of the intrigue and the tip of a hidden blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes secretive espionage and intrigue, typical of spy thrillers.

clue.text: Associations formed with canaille shaky at first

indicators.note: the letters are formed into a new shape
at first picks out the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Groups are created alongside a rabble that is unsteady to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: Canaille is French-derived for the rabble or riff-raff; 'formed' rearranges it into ALLIANCE, and the S from 'shaky at first' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Alliances are unions or associations formed for mutual benefit.

clue.text: Complete wreck

definitions.meaning: ... means complete or utter, as in ... failure

explanation.definitionFit: Total is both an adjective for utter or entire and a slang verb for writing off a vehicle.

clue.text: Very colourful — like actors on the cinema screen?

definitions.meaning: a ... character is flamboyant and colourful

definitions.text: like actors on the cinema screen?
definitions.meaning: literally, film actors are projected far bigger than real size

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means exaggeratedly vivid, and literally describes images bigger than actual size.

clue.text: Storm to trouble British sailors being sucked in

indicators.note: the sailors are drawn into the middle of the other pieces, as if inhaled

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble, as in 'much ado'
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's sailors

explanation.surface: A tempest causes difficulty as British seamen are dragged into its whirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' could be a verb, but it is the noun defined; 'being sucked in' places the sailors between the two other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, so a kind of storm.

clue.text: Search vigorously given time to find minor radical

parts.note: to rootle is to rummage or search vigorously, like a pig with its snout

explanation.surface: Someone digs about hard, given enough time, to unearth a minor political extremist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radical' suggests politics, but here it is botanical: a radical (or radicle) is a root.
explanation.definitionFit: A rootlet is a small root; radical in botany means arising from the root, so a minor root.

clue.text: Tree-dweller in shade endlessly

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the colour word is cut off

parts.note: orange is a shade or colour

explanation.surface: An animal lives up in the trees, forever in the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' suggests shadow, but it means a colour, ORANGE, losing its end letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An orang (orangutan) is a great ape that lives mostly in the forest canopy.

clue.text: In B&B need the whole bar

indicators.note: the word for need is placed inside the two B letters

parts.note: B&B gives the two letters B and B
lack means need or want
all means the whole of something

explanation.surface: A guest-house owner needs the entire bar to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but here it is a verb: to exclude.
explanation.definitionFit: To blackball is to vote against admitting someone to a club, so to bar or exclude them.

clue.text: Waxy substance, resin, alongside rigs at sea

indicators.note: the second piece is placed next to the first, after it

parts.note: amber is fossilised tree resin

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A waxy material and some resin wash up beside oil rigs out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy secretion from sperm whales, once prized in perfume making.

clue.text: Raven-keeper brings grouse to diner

parts.note: to grouse or beef is to complain
a diner is someone who eats, an eater

explanation.surface: A man who looks after ravens takes a game bird to a restaurant guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the game bird but is the verb meaning complain. Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders at the Tower of London, where ravens are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yeoman Warder at the Tower of London, including the Ravenmaster who tends the ravens there.

clue.text: Hotel in pleasant position

indicators.note: the hotel letter is placed inside the word for pleasant

parts.note: nice means pleasant
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel stands in an agreeable spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a suitable place or role, as in finding one's niche in life.

clue.text: Instruct goose soaring and circling to come down

indicators.note: the reversed bird goes round the landing word, enclosing it
in a down clue soaring means rising, so the bird's name reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: the nene is the Hawaiian goose
to light is to come down and settle, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: Teach a goose to fly up and circle before landing.
explanation.walkthrough: The nene is a Hawaiian goose, a crossword favourite; 'soaring' makes ENEN, which 'circling' wraps round the landing word.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlighten someone is to give them knowledge or understanding, to educate them.

clue.text: Saw things in Société Ethnologique?

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the French society's name, across the word break

explanation.surface: Members of a French anthropological society report sightings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw things' reads as hallucinating, but it means the things a saw has: its cutting points.
explanation.definitionFit: The teeth of a saw are the sharp points along its blade that do the cutting.

clue.text: Blissful soldier with youngster returning is embraced

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: the little word is held inside the reversed youngster, hugged by it
returning means the word for youngster is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a young boy

explanation.surface: A paratrooper is overjoyed to hug his son on his return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' makes DAL from the youngster, and 'is embraced' lets the clue's own 'is' serve as the piece held inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradisal means like paradise, heavenly, so supremely happy.

clue.text: Drug substitute in location — Bilbao's outskirts

parts.note: a place is a location

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A stand-in drug turns up somewhere on the edges of a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is an inert pill given instead of a real medicine, often in drug trials.

clue.text: Sink back — water at last to slip away

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of the word

parts.note: time elapses when it slips away

explanation.surface: Someone goes under, the water finally letting them slip from sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into a worse state, as of illness or bad habit.

clue.text: Inexperienced fellow mentioned stock market activity

parts.note: green means inexperienced or naive

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word sounds like the one for fellow

parts.note: a fellow is a male

explanation.surface: A naive man is spoken of in connection with dealings on the exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenmail is the practice of buying a large stake in a company and forcing it to buy the shares back at a premium.

clue.text: Result produced by plotters?

parts.note: plotters here are people plotting points, not conspirators

explanation.walkthrough: 'plotters' suggests conspirators, but those who plot points on axes produce a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph is a diagram made by plotting points or lines against axes.

clue.text: Joke about uniform left in labour camp

indicators.note: the joke word goes about the other letters, surrounding them

parts.note: a gag is a joke
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone jokes about the uniform worn in a prison camp.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulag was the Soviet system of forced-labour prison camps.

clue.text: Cold fish served up with hot worm

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means sent upwards, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A cold fish dish arrives along with a hot worm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns C and EEL into LEEC, before H is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a bloodsucking annelid, a kind of segmented worm.

clue.text: Scandinavian woman last in queue stretching across

parts.note: Astrid is a common Scandinavian woman's name

indicators.note: last in picks out the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A Nordic woman, last in the line, is reaching over.
explanation.definitionFit: To be astride something is to have legs spread over either side of it, spanning it.

clue.text: Serpent possibly existing now

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A snake may be alive today.
explanation.definitionFit: Present as an adjective means current, happening or existing at this time.

clue.text: Rowers hope to develop measure of strength

indicators.note: the letters develop, growing into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An eight's crew want to build up their power.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsepower is a unit measuring the power of an engine, so a gauge of strength.

clue.text: Something wrong swallowing hot piece of beef

indicators.note: the word for wrongdoing takes in the hot letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: There's a problem: someone gulped down a hot chunk of steak.
explanation.definitionFit: Shin is a cut of beef taken from the lower leg of the animal.
